product_problem: Daily Delhi commuters lack actionable intelligence to minimize inhaled pollution exposure during routine peak travel windows.

target.primary_prediction_target: Forward PM2.5 concentration (ug/m3) at station and corridor level for t+1h to t+6h horizons
target.derived_decision_target: Relative inhaled pollution dose (micrograms) calculated deterministically via concentration, duration, and metabolic ventilation rate
target.justification: PM2.5 accounts for >65% of air pollution health impacts in Delhi NCR, is monitored across 100% (42/42) of XKDR stations, and avoids mathematically lagging 24-hr multi-pollutant index artifacts.

data_sources.name: XKDR India Air Quality Database
data_sources.coverage: 42 CPCB CAAQM stations in Delhi NCR (2020-2024)
data_sources.limitations: Weather telemetry absent; AQI index absent; unit conversion required for CO.

data_sources.name: Open-Meteo Weather & Reanalysis API
data_sources.limitations: Grid-scale reanalysis (9-11 km) rather than micro-street intake.

data_sources.name: Copernicus CAMS
data_sources.role: Existing Phase 2 general regional baseline predictor.

station_strategy.strategy_name: Hybrid Station-Conditioned Model + Nearest Station Corridor Mapping
station_strategy.mechanism: Commuter corridors project onto physical CPCB monitors, providing transparent physical anchoring without black-box spatial hallucination.

model_strategy.leakage_controls: Strict chronological holdout splitting; zero future observational peeking; forward features restricted to NWP weather variables.

deterministic_components: EPA and INAQI sub-index category and color assignment
Inhaled dose calculation: Dose = Concentration * Ventilation_Rate * Duration
Mode ventilation constants: Walking (1.3 m3/h), Cycling (2.1 m3/h), Motorized (0.6 m3/h)
Haversine corridor distance and nearest station assignment
Departure window comparative argmin evaluation (t_0 vs t_0 + 30m vs t_0 + 60m)
Data freshness and sensor outage failover logic
ml_components: Multi-step forward particulate concentration forecasting (PM2.5 t -> t+k)
Meteorological dispersion response mapping under thermal inversion conditions

cost_constraints.policy: Strict zero-cost architecture using free/open public tiers and local caching only; zero cloud billing risks.

evaluation_strategy.spatial_holdout: Hold out 7 physical monitoring stations entirely to evaluate spatial transferability.

phase_3_stages.name: Observational Data Ingestion & Station Cache
phase_3_stages.scope: Ingest and structure multi-station time series for key Delhi corridors.

phase_3_stages.name: Corridor Geometry & Exposure Feature Engineering
phase_3_stages.scope: Define curated Delhi transit corridors and engineer lag/forecast feature tensors.

phase_3_stages.name: Station-Level Forecasting ML Engine
phase_3_stages.scope: Train, evaluate, and serialize forward PM2.5 forecasting model.

phase_3_stages.name: Deterministic Commuter Decision Engine
phase_3_stages.scope: Build physiological inhaled dose and departure shift comparator.

phase_3_stages.name: Backend API Extension
phase_3_stages.scope: Expose commuter endpoints with 100% backward compatibility for existing routes.

phase_3_stages.name: Commuter Advisor Frontend Integration
phase_3_stages.scope: Add departure time and corridor exposure decision dashboard.

phase_3_stages.name: Automated Testing & Security Verification
phase_3_stages.scope: Comprehensive test suite covering dose calculations, station queries, and security.

risks: Misinterpretation of personal exposure index as clinical medical advice
CPCB sensor outages during live demo (mitigated via local caching and nearest-station fallback)
Public API rate limiting on Open-Meteo (mitigated via client-side caching and static GeoJSON corridors)
open_questions: Should commuter corridors be pre-curated for the top 10 Delhi arterials or allow arbitrary coordinate inputs?
Should active transport (walking/cycling) ventilation multipliers be user-customizable?
Should both INAQI and EPA standards be toggled dynamically in the UI?
